title: Separation of India from Madagascar
summary: In the Late Cretaceous, volcanism along Madagascar's eastern margin accompanied the break-up of Madagascar from the Seychelles–India block. Argon dating gives about 87.6 million years for the lavas and dykes, and a recent study puts the second breakup near 90 million years ago. The Marion hotspot is widely linked to the event, though its exact role is debated.

uncertainty.note: 87.6 ± 0.6 Ma for dated eastern-margin volcanics (Storey et al. 1995); about 90 Ma in a 2025 review; other studies report volcanism spanning roughly 84–92 Ma (not opened).

where.modern_name: Androy, southern Madagascar (proposed Marion hotspot focus); breakup along the eastern margin
where.historical_name: No polities; Madagascar–Seychelles–India block in the Southern Indian Ocean

paleo.plate_model: MULLER2019 (Müller et al. 2019) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Other models at 88 Ma: MERDITH2021 44.52° S, 41.30° E; PALEOMAP 43.60° S, 35.76° E. Latitudes differ by about 4°, longitudes by up to 9°.

importance.justification: It isolated Madagascar and set India on its northward drift, shaping the island's unique fauna.
